subject: SOW term mechanics and buyer safeguards (BrightPath)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@brightpath.ai>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SOW term mechanics and buyer safeguards (BrightPath)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We put together a clean SOW + redline focused on term/renewal/termination mechanics per BrightPath’s ask. Two quick goals for sync:

- Make auto-renew predictable for both parties (cap on auto-renew length + earlier notice windows)
- Add buyer protection on termination for convenience / transition assistance and pro-rata refunds for unused committed capacity

Attached: BP_SOW_v3.pdf (clean) and redlines-MSA-BrightPath.docx (MSA redlines on term + data export).

High-level proposals in the SOW: 12-month initial term, auto-renews in 12-month increments but capped at two auto-renew cycles without express mutual agreement (i.e., max 36 months total unless renewed). Notice to opt-out: 60 days prior to renewal. Termination for convenience: allowed by customer with 60 days’ notice and a termination fee equal to 25% of remaining monthly committed fees or a pro-rated refund (whichever is lower).

Two items we need Legal to weigh in on (looping in Aditya & Laura):
1) Do we accept BrightPath’s ask for a 30-day cure period for material breach or insist on 14 days (we typically do 30 for enterprise deals).
2) Data export SLA on termination — BrightPath requests 90 days of complimentary export support; we typically offer 30 days and paid transition services after that.

Olivia — if those guardrails look directionally right, can you confirm the customer stakeholder who needs to approve the SOW (procurement + legal)? We’ll prep a version for signature.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachments: BP_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW), redlines-MSA-BrightPath.docx (MSA term redlines)

——

On Mon, 12 Apr 2027 at 11:03 AM PDT, Olivia Grant <olivia@brightpath.ai> wrote:
> From: Olivia Grant <olivia@brightpath.ai>
> To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
> Cc: procurement@brightpath.com
> Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: SOW term mechanics and buyer safeguards (BrightPath)
>
> Hi Marissa —
>
> Appreciate the quick turn. A few clarifications from our side: we like the capped auto-renew approach but need the opt-out window to be 45 days (our procurement calendar is tight). On termination for convenience we want 30 days’ notice with no termination fee for the first 12 months and a 30% fee thereafter.
>
> Also, for the cure period we proposed 30 days; legal at BrightPath is comfortable with that. On data export, 90 days complimentary is a hard requirement for our compliance team.
>
> Can your Legal and Finance confirm whether those items are acceptable or if we should expect counters?
>
> -Olivia
>
>
On Tue, 13 Apr 2027 at 10:07 AM PDT, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
> To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com
> Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
> Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:07:00 -0700
> Subject: RE: SOW term mechanics and buyer safeguards (BrightPath)
>
> Marissa / Olivia / Laura —
>
> Reviewing quick points:
>
> 1) Cure period: we can agree to 30 days for material breach in this deal line provided we add a backstop that if the breach relates to security or data exfiltration the cure period is 7 days and Redwood can suspend access immediately for safety. That gives BrightPath comfort and protects our platform.
>
> 2) Auto-renew cap / notice: 45 days is workable; I’ll propose 45 days in the redline for consistency with their procurement cycle. The cap at two auto-renews is OK.
>
> 3) Termination for convenience / fees: I don’t love a 30% fee after year one. Suggest a 25% sliding fee schedule: 0% within months 0–12, 15% within months 13–24, 25% thereafter. Also include an option for BrightPath to convert remaining committed spend to a 30-day notice with a service credit instead of paying the fee (gives them flexibility).
>
> 4) Data export: 90 days complimentary is a customer ask. We can do 90 days for small customers but for larger datasets we must include a reasonable assistance cap (e.g., up to 40 compute hours of export assistance included; additional hours billed). I’ll add language to the redline.
>
> 5) Pro-rata refund: confirm that any pre-paid committed credits are refundable pro-rata on termination for convenience net of applied fees. That’s standard and OK if Finance signs off.
>
> Laura — can you review the proposed suspension exception language for security-related incidents?
>
> Thanks,
>Aditya
>Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
>aditya.rao@redwood.com
>
>
On Wed, 14 Apr 2027 at 11:02 AM PDT, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
> To: Olivia Grant <olivia@brightpath.ai>
> Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
> Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
> Subject: RE: SOW term mechanics and buyer safeguards (BrightPath)
>
> Hi Olivia —
>
> Thanks — clear asks. We’ll send an updated redline with the following changes:
> - Opt-out/notice window set to 45 days (as requested)
> - Cure period set to 30 days with a 7-day exception for security/data incidents and explicit suspension rights for Redwood
> - Termination-for-convenience fee schedule adjusted to sliding 0% / 15% / 25% tiers (per Aditya); include conversion to service credit option
> - Data export: 90 days complimentary export assistance capped at 40 hours; additional hours billable at standard SOW rates
> - Refund mechanics: pre-paid committed credits refundable pro-rata net of applicable termination fee
>
> We’ll circulate the redlined MSA and SOW (redlines-MSA-BrightPath.docx and BP_SOW_v3.pdf) for final sign-off. Can BrightPath’s procurement confirm a 2-business-day review window once we send the DocuSign envelope? If agreed, we’ll aim to get this signed before the end of the month.
>
> Best,
>Marissa
